headline: Friendship founder Runa Khan wins Ramon Magsaysay Award
summary: The prestigious award, often called the 'Nobel Prize of Asia', recognizes her lifelong commitment to serving marginalized communities.
details: Runa Khan, the founder and executive director of the non-governmental organization Friendship, has been awarded the prestigious Ramon Magsaysay Award for 2026.
The Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation announced the winners in Manila, Philippines, on Monday, August 31.
Khan was selected for her leadership and dedication to serving people, creating opportunities for marginalized groups, and empowering the underprivileged to shape their own futures.
She shares the honor with Tommy Koh of Singapore and Bo Chi of Myanmar.
The award will be officially presented to her on November 15 at the Metropolitan Theater in Manila.
Established in 1957 to honor the memory of the seventh President of the Philippines, Ramon Magsaysay, the award is widely regarded as Asia's highest honor for greatness in public service.
Historically, the award was given in six specific categories, but since 2009, most categories have been open to a broader range of recipients.
caption:

The award will be officially presented to her on November 15 at the Metropolitan Theater in Manila.

headline_marked: Trump claims [[Iran's Kharg Island 'blown to smithereens']], but video is AI-generated
headline: Trump claims Iran's Kharg Island 'blown to smithereens', but video is AI-generated
summary: While the US struck rocket launchers on Larak Island, Iran retaliated by targeting US bases in Jordan with ballistic missiles.
details: US President Donald Trump claimed on social media that Iran's energy hub, Kharg Island, was being 'blown to smithereens,' accompanied by a video clip. However, Reuters confirmed the video was synthetically generated using AI software, and no other evidence of an attack on the island has emerged.

The conflict escalated after US forces carried out 'limited, precise' strikes against two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command stated the action was taken against minelaying forces that posed an 'imminent threat' to maritime security.

In retaliation, Iran launched ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan. Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting eight missiles, while Iranian state media claimed the attack caused casualties among soldiers and citizens.

Beyond military action, the US is intensifying economic pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that new secondary sanctions targeting banks will likely be unveiled weekly to further isolate the Iranian regime.

The tension has severely impacted global energy trade. Shipping data shows visible commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz dropped to just five a day over the weekend, as the waterway carries nearly a fifth of global crude oil and LNG shipments.
caption:
Trump claims an Iranian energy hub was 'blown to smithereens,' but the evidence was an AI-generated video.

US President Donald Trump claimed on social media that Iran's energy hub, Kharg Island, was being 'blown to smithereens,' accompanied by a video clip. However, Reuters confirmed the video was synthetically generated using AI software, and no other evidence of an attack on the island has emerged.

The conflict escalated after US forces carried out 'limited, precise' strikes against two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command stated the action was taken against minelaying forces that posed an 'imminent threat' to maritime security.

In retaliation, Iran launched ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan. Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting eight missiles, while Iranian state media claimed the attack caused casualties among soldiers and citizens.

Beyond military action, the US is intensifying economic pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that new secondary sanctions targeting banks will likely be unveiled weekly to further isolate the Iranian regime.

The tension has severely impacted global energy trade. Shipping data shows visible commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz dropped to just five a day over the weekend, as the waterway carries nearly a fifth of global crude oil and LNG shipments.
